description: What success is measured against. Captured at setup and framed into every forecast. Company and personal goals are tracked separately because they often differ — a rep can hit quota in a quarter the company misses, and a forecast that conflates them tells neither story.

columns.name: track
columns.note: Which motion this goal measures. New business and renewals are tracked as separate lines under the same owner because the work is not comparable — a renewal at 90% and a new deal at 90% require completely different effort. 'Total' exists only for an overall number that genuinely rolls both up, and should never be the only goal.

columns.name: period_label
columns.note: FY27, Q3-FY27, Aug-2026. Must match how the org names periods.

columns.name: original_target
columns.note: What it was when first set. Kept so a moved goal is visible as a moved goal rather than quietly becoming the number that was always there.

columns.name: revision_reason
columns.note: Why it moved. Territory change, reforecast, headcount, market.

columns.name: pace_required
columns.note: DERIVED: what still needs to close per remaining week to make it

columns.name: on_track
columns.note: DERIVED against elapsed time, not just raw attainment — 40% at the half is on track, 40% at three-quarters is not

columns.name: last_confirmed
columns.note: When the user last confirmed this is still the number. Goals drift; an unconfirmed goal quietly makes every forecast wrong.

columns.name: confirm_cadence
columns.note: Default Quarterly. The forecast skill re-asks when last_confirmed is older than this.

columns.name: status
columns.note: Superseded rather than deleted when a goal is replaced — mid-year changes are part of the story
